prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on where you are in Atlanta, your home/system type, budget, brands you prefer, and whether you value lowest price, longest warranty, or best workmanship.

To help you pick the best replacement contractor, here’s a practical plan plus a few well-known companies you can consider:

What to look for (must-haves)
- Valid Georgia HVAC license and insurance (liability + workers’ comp). Ask to see the license number.  
- Good recent local reviews (Google, Angi, Yelp) and few unresolved BBB complaints.  
- NATE-certified technicians and manufacturer training for the brand they install.  
- Written, itemized estimates with model numbers, SEER ratings, efficiency specs, labor, permits, and disposal of the old unit.  
- A Manual J load calculation (not just a rule-of-thumb) to size the system properly.  
- Clear warranty: manufacturer parts warranty, and at least 1–10 years on labor/installation depending on company.  
- Permit and inspection included.  
- References for recent installs (ask for 2–3 local homeowners).

Common reputable options in Atlanta (start your shortlist)
- Coolray (large regional company with many installs and service options).  
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin / Van Haaften family of franchises (local franchise networks like One Hour often have strong response times).  
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (national franchise with local presence).  
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (large national service network, often used for replacements).  

(These are examples — look up local franchise branches and read recent reviews for the specific branch in your neighborhood.)

How to get the best deal/installation
1. Get 3 written bids from different contractors.  
2. Make sure each bid uses the same scope (same system performance, same ductwork/coil needs, same removal cost, same warranty terms).  
3. Compare total cost, estimated energy savings (SEER), and warranty coverage — not just sticker price.  
4. Ask about rebates (utility or manufacturer) and available financing.  
5. Confirm timeline for delivery/installation and whether they’ll check/repair ducts, refrigerant charge, and airflow after install.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J and provide the report?  
- Which brands/models do you recommend for my home and why?  
- What is the total installed price and what’s included/excluded?  
- What are the labor and manufacturer warranties? Are extended warranties available?  
- Do you handle permits and inspections?  
- Can you provide local references and recent photos of similar installs?  
- How do you size the system and will you test airflow and refrigerant charge after install?

If you want, I can:
- Find the top-rated HVAC contractors near your Atlanta ZIP code and summarize recent reviews, or  
- Draft an email/phone script you can use to request quotes and ask the right questions, or  
- Help compare 3 estimates side-by-side if you paste them here.

Tell me your ZIP code, what kind of system you have now (central AC, heat pump, age), and any brand or budget preferences, and I’ll give more specific recommendations.
